transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I keep losing track of what I’m supposed to be working on and can’t seem to stay organized with all the tickets and follow-ups at my job. It’s gotten to the point where it’s causing some really serious issues for me at work, and I just feel completely overwhelmed trying to keep up.
Did you also have these kinds of attention or organization problems as a child, and do you ever feel unusually restless, fidgety, or impulsive?

Yes, even as a kid, my teachers wrote notes home about me daydreaming and blurting out answers, and I could never sit still long enough to finish my homework. Now, I'm constantly jiggling my leg or clicking pens, feel this pent-up energy in long meetings, and often cut people off mid-sentence because I get so impatient.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive/combined presentation, with symptoms beginning in childhood and persisting into adulthood. He reports chronic inattention and disorganization causing clear occupational impairment, plus hyperactive/impulsive features including fidgeting, restlessness, impatience, and interrupting others.
